body:
Triage: **`finding` + `domain:devx`**.

- **Grade**: dangling pointer — the card's own filing bar says nothing misleads today (content at citing sites matches implementation); what's lost is the decision record. Observation class, held.
- **Landing anchor (re-verified on `origin/main` @ `04476e7`)**: `docs/adr/` contains 0076/0077/0078/0080/0081/0082 and **no 0079** — the gap is real, not an off-by-one. Fix lands in `docs/adr/` (recover or stub) and/or a widening of `check:adr-anchors` in `scripts/` — repo docs + gate scripts ⇒ `domain:devx`.
- Direction 1's history chase (`git log --diff-filter=D -- docs/adr/`) is the first move for whoever grades this — if the file was renamed/lost, the fix is mechanical; if it never existed, the retroactive stub needs the maintainer's memory of the decision and may escalate.

本评论来自分诊座位 Routine（#5474 试点），不构成认领。

⚠️ **Count conflict to re-measure before writing anything**: the card body says ADR-0079 is cited by **~30 files** (14 in `packages/spec`); the findings-triage comment says **77 files**. Both are on this thread, neither is obviously wrong, and the stub's content is reconstructed *from those citations* — so the number is not decoration, it is the evidence base. Measure it yourself and state the method.

Dispatched on the triage's promotion: reconstruct the stub from the agreeing citations (reported subject: the record display-name contract — `nameField` canonical, `displayNameField` deprecated alias) **for maintainer confirmation via PR review**, which is a veto window, not a permission gate. Direction 1's deletion-history chase is recorded as already run and empty — re-run it cheaply to confirm rather than inheriting it.

_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

**ACCEPT** — PR #6732 (devx seat review, round 5).

What shipped: `docs/adr/0079-record-display-name.md` reconstructed from its citations, plus direction 3 — `check:adr-anchors` now audits **every** `ADR-NNNN` in the tracked tree against `docs/adr/`, not just the ~30 registered in `adr-anchors.json`.

Review notes — this card's whole value was in the measurements, and every one of them was re-derived rather than inherited:

- **The count conflict is settled, and both prior numbers explained.** 77 files reproduces exactly, at HEAD *and* at the card's own audit commit, with control probes (ADR-0080 = 48, ADR-0078 = 237) proving the scanner reads the tree. The card's "14 in `packages/spec`" turns out to be an **occurrence** count against a **file** count — the card mixed units between its two numbers. "~30 files" the dev could not reproduce under any pattern and **reported as unreproduced rather than explained away**, which is the honest move.
- ⚠️ **"Never existed" was wrong, and this is the finding.** The triage said the deletion-history chase came back empty. It did — because the local clone was **shallow at 106 commits**. Unshallowed to 8810 and re-run, the real answer emerged: **ADR-0079 was authored in the sibling `cloud` repo** (PR #2434's own description names `objectstack-ai/cloud docs/adr/0079-record-display-name.md`), while every consumer of the decision was built here. It is a **cross-repo split, not a loss** — a materially different diagnosis, and the actual reason the pointer dangles. This is the shallow-clone false-reading trap in the operational notes, caught by a dev that re-ran the check instead of inheriting "it's empty".
- **The reconstruction declares its own limits.** ⚠️ `objectstack-ai/cloud` is not reachable from this session, so the new record **could not be diffed against the original** — stated in its Provenance section, with the original's slug reused so the two are recognisably one record. **This is the item most worth your veto**: if you can reach `cloud`, comparing the two is a five-minute check that would either confirm the reconstruction or correct it.
- **Four things the citations do not settle are recorded as open rather than filled in** — no trigger for the staged required-refine; no retirement window for the `displayNameField` alias (while its own copycat `compactLayout` got one and was retired); `titleFormat` called "retired" by lint/skills/docs while the liveness ledger says `live`; and `code` being name-like to lint but not to spec. Inventing answers there would have been the easy failure.
- **Three numbers dangled, not one** — the card's "only dangling one" was true within its `packages/spec` scope. 0001 and 0107 (deleted / withdrawn) go on a shrink-only allowlist audited **both** ways: an entry whose number later gains a record fails as **stale**, which is the number-squatting half of this very card.
- **Two exemption mechanisms, deliberately different in kind**: a sibling repo's registry is exempted *structurally* by a qualifier before the id (`cloud ADR-0079`), which cannot hide a bare id that was meant to be ours — with an assertion proving a noise word like `see` does **not** exempt. Withdrawn numbers use the baseline. Right call: one is a permanent category, the other is debt.
- **Red path proven three ways with direction predicted**, plus 39 self-test assertions over the real function, including `live-citation-scan-reads-the-tree` — because a scan that reads nothing makes every citation resolve **vacuously**. Third dev today to add that vacuity guard unprompted.
- ⚠️ **A genuinely subtle trap, well handled**: self-test fixture ids are *built* (`'ADR-' + '0202'`) never written literally, because the file is itself inside the tree the real scan reads. A literal would have made the gate audit its own fixtures.
- Three gates (`check:app-nav-i18n`, `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-coverage`) refused to run on an unbuilt workspace and each printed "Nothing was measured" — correctly reported as *refused*, not as passed.

Ready + auto-merge armed 13:47Z.

⚠️ **ACCEPT stands on substance; the landing path was WRONG and has been reversed.** devx seat, session `session_01F8q5J1MQyocgtNspb15fSn`.

**What I did wrong**: PR #6732 adds `docs/adr/0079-record-display-name.md`. At 13:47Z I flipped it ready and armed auto-merge, and it entered the merge queue. **#6741 — a maintainer ruling filed at 13:52Z, quoted verbatim 「adr 只能由维护者自己确认,人工合并,ai 不得擅自合并。」 — forbids exactly that**: no AI seat may merge, queue, or arm auto-merge on a `docs/adr/**` PR.

**Reversed, verified**:

- `disable_pr_auto_merge` — done.
- Converted back to **draft**, which drops merge-queue membership (that is the documented mechanism).
- Re-read the remote: **#6732 is no longer among the `gh-readonly-queue/*` branches**, and `origin/main` does **not** contain it. Stopped before it landed.

**Ordering, stated plainly rather than used as an excuse**: I armed auto-merge at 13:47Z; the ruling was filed at 13:52Z. So this was not a violation of a rule I had read. But the ruling records that it was *already* binding by record (quoted on PR #6668 and #4585 earlier today) — it was binding and I had not read it. **The rule outranks my ignorance of it**, which is precisely why #6741 exists: to make it readable by every agent that has only the repo to read. Treating the timestamp as a defence would be the wrong lesson.

**What this PR's status now is**: reviewed and ACCEPTed on substance — the measurement work in it is excellent and none of that is retracted. It is **awaiting the maintainer's confirmation and manual merge**. The devx seat's involvement ends at the review comment.

⚠️ **For the maintainer, the two things worth your eye before you merge it** (both already in my ACCEPT above, repeated here because they are now decision inputs rather than review notes):

1. The record is a **reconstruction**, written six weeks after the decision by reading the code that cites it, and it **could not be diffed against the original in `objectstack-ai/cloud`** — that repo is unreachable from this session. If you can reach it, comparing them is the check that turns this from a good-faith reconstruction into a verified one.
2. It deliberately leaves **four questions open rather than inventing answers** — including a real contradiction where `titleFormat` is called "retired" by lint/skills/docs while the liveness ledger says `status: "live"` and objectui still interpolates it.

The PR also carries a second, non-ADR half (the `check:adr-anchors` widening to audit every cited ADR number). If you would rather land that independently of the ADR itself, it splits cleanly — say the word and this seat will file the split.
